name: GSM-Hard
summary: 1,319 grade-school math problems with larger quantities.
overview: GSM-Hard changes quantities in GSM8K problems to make arithmetic more demanding while keeping the word-problem format. The PAL paper introduced the variant to study how model accuracy changes when some numbers become much larger. [PAL paper](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/gao23f.html)
methodology: This snapshot includes all 1,319 problems in the authors' `gsmhardv2.jsonl` release. Each task presents the original `input` field and stores its numeric `target`. Keys are one-based line numbers. Benchopedia uses direct numeric responses with the paper's answer comparison. [Pinned dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/reasoning-machines/gsm-hard/blob/960448f73503112d4226baeb8eb41d3fb5ae2506/gsmhardv2.jsonl), [Original release commit](https://github.com/reasoning-machines/pal/commit/9a51009fc45ab99b35955b49d89ba6091a904036)
scoring: A numeric answer is correct when its absolute difference from the target is less than 0.001. Accuracy is the fraction of all questions answered correctly. [PAL evaluation script](https://github.com/reasoning-machines/pal/blob/f81ca2a9777f002f98a6b4d0f10b61bd5c8feb02/scripts/gsm_eval.py)
limitations: The examples inherit the language and subjects of GSM8K. The paper compares multiple methods, including generated programs evaluated by a Python runtime. Direct numeric predictions use a different generation method. [PAL paper](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/gao23f.html)
